title: Risotto allo zafferano
subtitle: Saffron risotto without the bone marrow
excerpt: Risotto allo zafferano is the simple saffron risotto: the rice is cooked in chicken or vegetable stock and finished with saffron, butter, and Parmesan. It is lighter than the milanese version and makes an elegant first course or a side dish for braised meats. The golden colour comes entirely from the saffron.
sourceNotes: Northern Italian home-cooking tradition. A simpler version of risotto alla milanese, without bone marrow. Saffron-scented risotto is eaten across Lombardy and Piedmont as a standalone dish or alongside roast meats. Method from Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking (1992).

content.text: Risotto allo zafferano is the straightforward saffron risotto: a creamy, golden rice dish made with chicken or vegetable stock, steeped saffron, and finished with cold butter and Parmesan. It makes a good starter or a side dish for roast chicken, braised lamb, or any meat with its own sauce. Steep the saffron in warm stock for at least 10 minutes before adding it to the rice.

items.prepNote: steeped in 3 tbsp warm stock for 10 minutes
half for cooking, half cold for finish

content.text: Steep {{saffron}} of saffron in 3 tablespoons of warm stock for 10 minutes. Keep the remaining {{stock-chicken}} of stock hot in a small pan.

Melt 40 g of the butter in a wide heavy pan over medium-low heat. Cook the shallots gently for 8 minutes. Add {{arborio-rice}} of rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains are lightly toasted. Pour in {{dry-white-wine}} of wine and stir until absorbed.
Add the saffron with its liquid, then continue adding hot stock one ladle at a time over 18 minutes, stirring regularly. Stop when the rice is al dente.
Remove from the heat. Beat in the remaining 40 g of cold butter and the Parmesan. Season, cover, rest 2 minutes, then serve immediately.

items.cause: Not enough stock, or rested too long before serving.
items.fix: Add more hot stock and stir through just before serving. Risotto sets quickly once off the heat.

items.cause: Saffron was not steeped long enough, or too little used.
items.fix: A full 10-minute steep in warm liquid is non-negotiable. The colour deepens with time.

content.text: Saffron risotto is the main rice dish of Lombardy and Piedmont, where risotto is everyday food. The simpler zafferano version (without bone marrow) is what home cooks make on a weeknight alongside a roast chicken. The colour matters as much as the flavour: a deep golden risotto tells you the saffron was properly steeped.
